skill.name: remove-animations
skill.description: Review existing interface animations, remove unnecessary motion, reduce distracting effects, and clean up unused animation code while checking behavior dependencies.
skill.summary: Remove unnecessary interface motion while preserving useful feedback and checking removal hazards.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Excessive interface motion can delay frequent tasks and distract from useful information. This skill guides targeted removals, smaller effects, and cleanup while checking behavior dependencies.
actual_capabilities: Inspect CSS, Tailwind utilities, and Motion props for existing interface animations.
Classify animations for removal, reduction, or retention using trigger, frequency, purpose, and duration.
Check hidden start states, completion callbacks, unmount timing, focus timing, and layout dependencies before removal.
Remove unnecessary motion and simplify excessive entrances, hover effects, staggers, and persistent loops.
Clean up unused keyframes, wrappers, variants, imports, and animation configuration.
Report changes, deliberately retained animations, verification results, and proposed dependency removal.
limitations: Does not add new animations or repair easing, origin, or interruptibility for animations that should remain.
Does not fix underlying layout shifts; affected animations should remain with the layout issue reported.
Requires approval before removing a motion dependency or changing its lockfile entries.
Cannot determine every interaction quality from source alone; device checks and existing project tests may be necessary.

use_cases.title: Simplify Frequent Dashboard Interactions
use_cases.description: Remove repeated tab, navigation, and data entrance animations while preserving feedback that communicates real changes.

use_cases.title: Reduce Decorative Website Motion
use_cases.description: Review repeated scroll reveals, card hover transforms, and persistent loops while preserving purposeful marketing animation.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Animation Refactors
use_cases.description: Check callbacks, focus handling, unused imports, and remaining references after animation removal.

prompt_templates.title: Remove One Distracting Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Remove the unnecessary hover scale from my project cards. Check dependencies and preserve useful interaction feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Frequent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our command palette and tab navigation. Remove unnecessary motion, check focus and close behavior, and report what you kept.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit dashboard animations by trigger, frequency, and purpose. Apply removals and reductions, check hazards, and run available tests and type checks.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Motion Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing motion across this app. Apply justified removals and reductions, preserve documented decisions, and clean orphaned code. Request approval before dependency removal.

output_examples.input: The command palette feels delayed when opened with a shortcut.
output: Removed the opening and closing animation because the interaction is keyboard-triggered.
Moved focus handling from animation completion to the opening action.
Retained the occasional toast entrance because it communicates where the notification appears.

output_examples.input: Reduce repeated scroll effects on our product website.
output: Removed repeated section reveals and their hidden initial states.
Retained the primary hero entrance because it supports the page explanation.
Removed unused reveal styles and observer logic. Listed remaining device checks.

output_examples.input: Clean up the code left after removing dashboard animations.
output: Removed unused keyframes, animation imports, and empty motion wrappers.
Updated tests that waited for animation completion.
Proposed removing the unused motion dependency, pending approval.

best_practices: Provide interaction frequency and product context before judging which animations should remain.
Check visibility, callbacks, unmount behavior, focus, and layout before removing an effect.
Run available project checks and review perceived speed on a real device.
anti_patterns: Delete every transition without checking its purpose or documented design decision.
Remove an animation while leaving hidden start states or completion-dependent behavior.
Uninstall a motion dependency without approval or confirmation that no imports remain.

faq.question: Does this skill remove every animation?
faq.answer: No. It preserves purposeful motion, including feedback, spatial context, and occasional first-time moments.

faq.question: Can it work with CSS and Motion components?
faq.answer: Yes. Its workflow covers CSS transitions, keyframes, Tailwind animation utilities, Motion props, and related wrappers.

faq.question: Does it add or redesign animations?
faq.answer: No. It removes or reduces existing effects and reports retained animations that need separate improvement.

faq.question: How does it check for removal regressions?
faq.answer: It checks hidden states, callbacks, unmount timing, focus, layout shifts, and affected tests before verifying available project checks.

faq.question: Will it uninstall an unused animation library?
faq.answer: It proposes dependency removal and asks for approval before uninstalling the library.

faq.question: Can it guarantee that the interface feels faster?
faq.answer: No. Source review cannot establish every perceptual result, so interaction quality may require real-device checks.
